# PatternCard

Card pattern for PLUS design system. Mirrors Figma `Pattern/Card`: an optional image, then the content (the `_Card header` over the body), then an optional footer, on Atlassian's raised pair: the raised surface and its shadow, whose 1px ring is the card's edge. - **Layout**: `stacked` (default) puts the image above the content. `image-start` and `image-end` put it beside the content, content two thirds and image one third, for wide cards; below the md breakpoint (768) a side card stacks. One layout per row of cards. - **Header** (`_Card header`): `title` (the card title type, shared with Card in `styles/_card-title.scss`, one heading level below its section) over an optional `description` (Body/default 14), with `actions` at the end of the row. `header` replaces that block with custom content, like the header's `custom` type, for tabs or a toolbar. - **Spacing** comes from the Card tokens: `padding` sets Card/pad-sm · md · lg, the header sits Card/stack-md above the body (`gap` picks the stack step), and the footer sits Card/stack-lg below. The footer is left-aligned. - The card hugs its content; in a row it stretches to the tallest card. - **Elevation**: the raised pair at rest. A card with an `onClick` lifts on hover to the raised surface's hovered step under the overlay shadow, and settles back onto the raised shadow while pressed; `dragging` puts any card on the overlay pair while it moves. The card also sets the current surface, so a sticky table cell inside it matches the card.

Also asked as: summary card, object card.

**Import:** `import { PatternCard } from '@/patterns';`

## Usage

Use a card when one object needs its own container on the page. A card holds a heading, some content and, when people can act on it, a footer. This template is the shell: you fill its slots with your own parts.

Build a card in four steps. Pick the size by what it holds. Choose the header, or turn it off when the body carries its own title. Fill the body slot, spacing only inside the slot content with the Card stack tokens. Add the footer only for actions that commit.

### Size guidance

Content picks the size. Choose the smallest card that holds the content without clipping, then let the row decide how many fit. Height always hugs the content, and a card in a row stretches to the tallest card.

| Size | When to use | Pad | Radius | Minimum width | Height cap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sm` | One number or one line. | 16 | 12 | 224 | 304 |
| `md` | A short list or a few lines. | 20 | 16 | 304 | 400 |
| `lg` | A summary with several parts. | 24 | 16 | 480 | 640 |

In Figma, `size` picks the pad, the radius and the minimum width together. In code, `padding` sets the pad and the radius, and `minWidth` sets the minimum width. A height cap is set with `style`'s `maxHeight`, and the card clips what passes it.

### Cards in a row

In a row, place the most cards that keep each card at its minimum width. Each row is the content width of its mode, with a 16 gutter. The count switches between viewport widths of 1224 and 1256 with the sidebar docked.

| Mode | Content width | Small, 224 | Medium, 304 | Large, 480 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Medium, 768 | 720 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| Large, 1024 | 736 | 3 | 2 | 1 |
| X-Large, 1440 | 1152 | 4 | 3 | 2 |

## Motion

PatternCard reads these motion tokens and no literal duration or curve.

| Event | Transition | Tokens | What it does | Sound |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| change | Update a value or state | `--ds-motion-appearance-fast` | It changes color on hover and press like a Button. Opening a clickable card is Drill. |  |
| milestone | Opening a page | `--ds-motion-spatial-default` | The one card in a milestone page entrance is Expressive and leaves by the exit rules. | `sound.done.milestone` on land: onboarding complete, first session, goal reached, term start or end, badge claimed; goal reached is shared, so the student hears it |

## Best practices

### Size the card to what it holds. {#size-the-card-to-what-it-holds}

Visible empty space inside the card means size down. A clipped or crowded body means size up.

Do: One number fits sm. The card is only as wide as it needs, so a row of them stays tidy.
Don't: The same number in lg leaves most of the card empty. Size down instead of filling the space.

### Never put a card inside a card. {#never-put-a-card-inside-a-card}

A card's raised fill and shadow are its own object boundary. Group related cards in a Section instead.

Do: One card; three metrics stacked in its body, split by dividers.
Don't: Three mini cards inside the card. Borders and shadows pile up and the hierarchy flattens.

### Keep the card in place while it loads. {#keep-the-card-in-place-while-it-loads}

Do: Loading keeps the card in place: a skeleton fills the body, so the layout does not jump when data arrives.
Don't: A bare loading line takes the card away. The row collapses and everything below it moves.

### Put commit actions in the footer. {#put-commit-actions-in-the-footer}

A card that holds actions that commit a change gets a footer, and its actions start on the left, under the content. Only a modal footer aligns right.

## Accessibility

- The title is a heading one level below the section the card sits in: an h3 in a section, an h2 straight on a page. Nest the card in a Section rather than choosing a tag.
- A card that is clickable as a whole needs a role and a tab stop, and it must answer Enter and Space. When the card has one action, put a Button in the footer instead.
- Mark the card `aria-busy` while it loads. The skeleton bars are hidden from assistive technology.
- The hover lift is never the only cue that a card is clickable. Pair it with a visible action or a link in the card.
- Text sits on the raised surface in `--ds-text` and `--ds-text-subtle`, which meet contrast in every color mode.
- The card sets the current surface to its raised fill, so a sticky table cell inside it matches the card.

- Modal for something that must be decided before the page can continue.

## Parts

1. **Image** (optional). A slot above everything else, or beside the content in a side layout. It runs edge to edge, outside the pad, and the card radius clips its corners. Stacked, give the image you pass an aspect ratio of 16:9, 4:3 or 1:1; beside the content it fills the full height at one third of the width and crops to cover.
2. **Header.** The title, an optional description and an optional actions slot. A custom `header` replaces all three. In Figma the title truncates to one line and the description's `text` variant truncates at three lines or wraps; code leaves wrapping to CSS.
3. **Body.** A slot for text, a list or media.
4. **Footer** (optional). A left-aligned slot for actions that commit a change.

The image sits above (or, in a side layout, beside) a padded frame, and the header, body and footer sit inside it.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The raised pair: `--ds-surface-raised` with `--ds-shadow-raised`. |
| Hovered | A clickable card only: `--ds-surface-raised-hovered` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`. A card with no `onClick` does not change. |
| Pressed | A clickable card only: `--ds-surface-raised-pressed` with `--ds-shadow-raised`. |
| Focused | The card has no focus style of its own. A card made clickable as a whole takes `role` and `tabIndex` from you. |
| Disabled | A card is never disabled. Disable the controls inside it. |
| Dragging | `--ds-surface-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`, held under hover and press. |
| Loading | Skeleton bars in the body, with `aria-busy` on the card. Figma's `loading?` has no prop in code. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Title the card with the object it holds, in sentence case: "Ana Ruiz", "Sessions this week". | A generic title such as "Details" or "Info". |
| Keep the description to one line that adds something, such as "Lincoln Middle · Thu 4:00 PM". | A description that repeats the title. |
| Name a footer action for what it does: "Save note", "View session". | "OK" or "Submit". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | — |
| `title` | node | — | The card's title, in the card title type (`styles/_card-title.scss`), tagged one heading level below its section |
| `description` | node | — | Body/default 14 under the title |
| `actions` | node | — | Actions at the end of the header row: buttons, a pager or an overflow |
| `header` | node | — | Custom header that replaces title, description and actions (tabs, a toolbar) |
| `image` | node | — | Image slot, full bleed: above the content, or at the start or end edge per `layout` |
| `layout` | enum | `'stacked'` | Where the image sits. `stacked` puts it above the content. `image-start` and `image-end` put it beside the content at one third of the width, full height, bleeding to the card's top, bottom and that side's edge; for wide cards, and below the md breakpoint they stack. |
| `footer` | node | — | Footer slot: commit actions, left-aligned, Card/stack-lg below the body |
| `padding` | enum | `'md'` | Padding scale: Card/pad-sm · md · lg (16 · 20 · 24) |
| `gap` | enum | `'md'` | Header-to-body stack: Card/stack-sm · md · lg (4 · 8 · 12) |
| `minWidth` | number or string | — | Minimum width constraint (number of px or any CSS length) |
| `onClick` | func | — | Click handler, passed to the card's root element. Its presence adds the clickable class: a pointer cursor and the hover lift. It adds no role or tab stop; pass `role` and `tabIndex` for a card clickable as a whole. |
| `onKeyDown` | func | — | Key handler, passed to the card's root element. A card clickable as a whole takes Enter and Space here, beside its `role` and `tabIndex`. |
| `dragging` | bool | `false` | The card is being dragged: it lifts to the overlay pair |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
| `style` | object | — | — |
| `children` | node | — | Body content slot |

## Variants

**`layout`** — `stacked` · `image-start` · `image-end`

**`padding`** — `sm` · `md` · `lg`

The named string values each prop takes. A prop's full type is in Props: a prop listed here may also take a boolean or a number, and a prop missing here may still have named values.
